subject: Money
title: Public Goods Problem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Public Goods Problem.

hook.text: A lighthouse benefits every ship that passes. But no single ship owner would pay to build one alone.

buildup.text: Public goods are things everyone uses but nobody can be excluded from: defense, clean air, streetlights.

discovery.text: Free-rider problem: if you can benefit without paying, you won't pay. So nobody pays. So nothing gets built.

twist.text: Taxes solve the free-rider problem by making everyone contribute. Compulsion replaces volunteerism.

climax.text: Without taxes, many essential services would vanish. Markets alone can't fund what everyone shares.

quiz.question: What is the free-rider problem?
options: People using public transit for free
Benefiting from public goods without contributing
